questions.question_text: In a quadrilateral, one diagonal bisects the other at right angles, but the two diagonals do not bisect each other. Which quadrilateral is it?

options.text: Kite
Rhombus
options.why: In a rhombus both diagonals are bisected, not just one of them.

options.text: Square
options.why: In a square both diagonals are bisected and are also equal in length.

options.text: Trapezium
options.why: A trapezium has no diagonal property at all, so nothing is bisected.

questions.question_text: Which statement about the angles of a rhombus is always true?

options.text: Opposite angles are equal.
All four angles are right angles.
options.why: Applies a square property to every rhombus, but a rhombus need not have right angles.

options.text: Adjacent angles are equal.
options.why: Would force all four angles to be equal, which only happens for a square.

options.text: All four angles are different.
options.why: Ignores that a rhombus is a parallelogram, whose opposite angles must match.

questions.solution_text:
A rhombus has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so the angles at opposite corners match.
Opposite angles are equal.

questions.question_text: Which diagonal property does a square have that a rhombus need not have?

options.text: The two diagonals are equal in length.
The diagonals cross at right angles.
options.why: Every rhombus already has perpendicular diagonals, so this separates nothing.

options.text: The diagonals bisect the vertex angles.
options.why: Every rhombus already has angle-bisecting diagonals, so this separates nothing.

options.text: The diagonals meet at the centre of the shape.
options.why: The diagonals of every rhombus already meet at its centre, so this separates nothing.

questions.solution_text:
A rhombus already has perpendicular, angle-bisecting diagonals that cut each other in half.
Only the square must also have its two diagonals equal in length.

questions.question_text: Which diagonal property does a rhombus have that a kite need not have?

options.text: Both diagonals are cut in half at the crossing point.
The diagonals meet at a right angle.
options.why: True of every kite as well, so it separates nothing.

options.why: True of every kite as well, since the axis bisects the other diagonal.

options.text: One diagonal bisects two of the vertex angles.
options.why: True of every kite as well, since the axis bisects the angles it passes through.

In a kite only the shorter diagonal is bisected; in a rhombus each diagonal cuts the other in half.
Both diagonals are cut in half at the crossing point.
